defs.def: to break open or apart, especially because of pressure from inside; to make sth break in this way （使）爆裂，胀开

ex.s: Susan burst into tears after her baby's operation because she was ______.
ex.t: 苏珊在宝宝手术后大哭是因为她______。

defs.def: to go or move somewhere suddenly with great force; to come from somewhere suddenly 猛冲；突然出现

ex.s: In the 1980s, the team burst onto the international volleyball scene with several major world titles, and an amazing three-set victory over the United States in the final of the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.
ex.t: 20世纪80年代，这支球队突然在国际排坛崭露头角，赢得了几个重要的世界冠军，并在1984年洛杉矶奥运会决赛中以惊人的三比零战胜美国。

defs.def: to be very full of sth; to be very full and almost breaking open 爆满；涨满
to speak suddenly, loudly and with strong feeling 突然激动地喊叫

ex.s: I was also caught up in the excitement and cheered so hard that I thought my lungs would burst!
ex.t: 我也被这激动人心的氛围所感染，拼命欢呼，以为我的肺会爆炸！

defs.def: to begin doing sth suddenly 突然开始（做某事）
a short period of a particular activity or strong emotion that often starts suddenly 突发；猝发；迸发；爆破

ex.s: Little do they know that as they do so, a burst of energy is sent up to street level to help charge an electric car.
ex.t: 他们几乎不知道，在这么做的同时，一股能量被传送到街道层面，用来给一辆电动汽车充电。

defs.def: an occasion when sth bursts; the hole left where sth has burst 爆裂；裂口

ex.s: It burst into hundreds of pieces.
As the “lucky” name was ___45___, the class burst into laughter.
ex.t: 当“幸运”这个名字被____45____时，全班爆发出笑声。

ex.s: (All the other HAPPINESSES burst out laughing.) Why, we are the only things you do know!
ex.t: （所有其他“幸福”都大笑起来。）哎呀，我们才是你唯一确有所知的东西！

ex.s: (All the HAPPINESSES burst out laughing.) THE HAPPINESS: You heard him!
ex.t: （所有“幸福”都大笑起来。）幸福：你听见他说的了！

defs.def: a short series of shots from a gun 一阵短促的射击

ex.t: 林的观众爆发出一阵笑声。

ex.s: By 9:33am, a burst of additional traffic might push it to 145 seconds.
ex.t: 到上午9:33，一阵额外的车流可能把它推高到145秒。
